clue.text: Disturbing a French kid he produces a nose rag

definitions.note: a jokey name for the cloth you blow your nose on

indicators.note: disturbing these words throws their letters out of order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A boy upset in France pulls out something to wipe his nose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disturbing' rearranges all twelve letters of A FRENCH KID HE; 'produces' links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang synonym: a nose rag is the cloth square carried in a pocket for blowing one's nose.

clue.text: Book house overlooking ocean

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece overlooking another sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: the sea is an ocean

explanation.surface: An estate agent's listing for a house with a sea view.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: it is one of the books of the Old Testament, named after a minor prophet.

clue.text: Rule again, suffering spasmodic pain

indicators.note: letters that are suffering have been knocked about, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A ruler forced back into power is in agony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering' rearranges the letters of RULE AGAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Medical term: it names sharp, intermittent pain along the course of a nerve.

clue.text: Person teasing cleric, one leaving Worcs town

parts.note: a kidder is someone who kids, i.e. teases

indicators.note: the letter standing for one is leaving, so it is dropped from the pieces

parts.note: a minister is a clergyman
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A joker mocking a vicar who is departing a Midlands town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one leaving' drops an I from the cleric. Worcs is short for Worcestershire, an English county; the town is famous for carpets.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: it is a market town in Worcestershire, in the English West Midlands.

clue.text: Deliver poem perhaps about spectacle mentioned in speech

parts.note: re means about, concerning

indicators.note: a word mentioned in speech is heard rather than read, so we want a word that sounds like the synonym

parts.note: a sight is a spectacle

explanation.surface: A performer delivers a poem about some dramatic scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mentioned in speech' says SIGHT is heard, giving CITE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to deliver a poem from memory to an audience is to say it aloud by heart.

clue.text: Her sons cut the damaged tree

indicators.note: damaged letters are broken up and reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: A woman's boys lopped the tree and harmed it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges the thirteen letters of HER SONS CUT THE.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a large deciduous tree whose shiny brown nuts British children play conkers with.

clue.text: One reigning over a long period

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece over another sits above it and so comes first

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the queen, one reigning
taken as written; that the letters run on across 'over a' is coincidence, not a hidden word

explanation.surface: A monarch who ruled for many years.
explanation.walkthrough: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an epoch or age is a lengthy stretch of history.

clue.text: As well-placed models presumably are when sitting?

definitions.text: As well-placed models presumably are when sitting?

parts.words: As well-placed models presumably are when sitting?
parts.note: models are good-looking, so when they sit they are literally sitting attractive

explanation.surface: Models posing for a portrait are comfortably positioned.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'sitting pretty' means being in a comfortable, advantageous position; models are good-looking too.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom plus synonym: good-looking models sitting would be attractive, completing the phrase for being well off.

clue.text: Secure area of the sea

definitions.meaning: ... as an adjective means safe and solid, firmly secure
a ... is a narrow stretch of sea or inlet, like Puget ...

explanation.surface: A safe stretch of water.
explanation.definitionFit: Double definition: an adjective meaning firm and safe, and a noun for a strait or inlet.

clue.text: Buccaneer's reportedly indelicate manner

indicators.note: something reportedly so is passed on by word of mouth, so we want a word that sounds like this phrase

parts.note: coarse means indelicate or crude; an air is a manner or bearing

explanation.surface: A pirate is said to have a crude way about him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' says COARSE AIR is heard, giving the pirate.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both name a pirate, especially one raiding ships along the Barbary coast.

clue.text: Stories appearing in American anthologies

indicators.note: the letters are appearing inside these two words, straddling the gap between them

explanation.surface: Tales published in collections from the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appearing in' finds the letters across americAN Anthologies.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword-friendly sense: a collection of anecdotes, sayings or gossip about a person is called this.

clue.text: Beg to get church involved in ballet movement

indicators.note: the church is involved in, wrapped up inside, the word for beg

parts.note: to entreat is to beg

explanation.surface: Pleading to have a church take part in a dance step.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beg' looks like the verb of the surface, but it only supplies a synonym to be split open; 'to get' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a leap in ballet during which the dancer crosses the feet several times in the air.

clue.text: Fellow doctor supports beloved, a source of sweetness

indicators.note: in a down clue, the pieces that support another sit beneath it, so they come after

parts.note: honey is an endearment for a beloved
co-, as in co-worker, means fellow or joint
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A doctor colleague props up a sweetheart, who brings sweetness.
explanation.walkthrough: CO is the prefix meaning fellow, as in co-pilot.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: the wax cells built by bees are where their honey is stored, so it yields sweetness.

clue.text: High-ranking Asian woman say taken in by tramp

indicators.note: the abbreviation for say is taken in, enclosed, by the word for tramp

parts.note: bum is US slang for a tramp or vagrant
EG, for example, means say

explanation.surface: A noblewoman, for instance, is duped by a vagrant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' is the usual signal for an example abbreviation; 'tramp' is American slang here.
explanation.definitionFit: Title: in South Asia, a Muslim woman of high rank or a lady of status is given this honorific.

clue.text: Sort of lynx bishop caught in seagoing vessel

indicators.note: the two letters go in, inside, the word for a seagoing vessel

parts.note: a boat is a seagoing vessel
B is the chess notation for bishop
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A wild cat and a churchman are trapped aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Bishop and caught are both single-letter abbreviations, from chess and cricket scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the North American wildcat is a smaller relative in the lynx genus.

clue.text: Hard man with practical skills

parts.note: H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard
Andy is a man's name

explanation.surface: A tough guy who is good at DIY.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone good with their hands, clever at practical jobs, is described this way.

clue.text: Military policeman in preferred capacity

indicators.note: the letters are in, inside, these two words, running across the gap

explanation.surface: An army officer serving in the role he would choose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points at the letters across prefeRRED CAPacity.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang: military police wear red-topped caps, giving them this nickname.

clue.text: Stupid British artist getting out more?

parts.note: RA, a Royal Academician, is an artist
someone getting out more is at home, or in, less often

explanation.surface: A dim British painter who supposedly ought to socialise more.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful step: if you go out more, you are in less.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: having no brains, figuratively, means being foolish or dim.

clue.text: Churchyard tree the solver talked of

indicators.note: a word talked of is spoken, so we want the word that sounds like this

parts.note: the solver is you, the person reading the clue

explanation.surface: A tree in the graveyard that people mention to you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'talked of' says YOU is heard, giving the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: this evergreen conifer is traditionally planted in British churchyards.

clue.text: Grumble when husband gets in hock, perhaps

indicators.note: the husband's abbreviation gets in, inside, the drink word

parts.note: hock is a German white wine, so an example of wine

explanation.surface: A wife complains when her husband sneaks off for a German white.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets in' puts H inside WINE. Hock is a German white wine from the Rhine.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to complain in a peevish, nagging way is to moan or grumble.

clue.text: Austere knight leaves climb in Cairngorms, primarily

indicators.note: the knight leaves, so its letter is dropped from the word for climb

parts.note: an ascent is a climb
N is the chess notation for knight

indicators.note: primarily means taking the first, primary, letter of each word

explanation.surface: A stern knight sets off up a mountain in the Scottish Highlands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' drops N from ASCENT, leaving ASCET. The Cairngorms are a Scottish mountain range.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: practising severe self-denial, shunning comforts, is being austere.

clue.text: Endlessly stylish Greek character

indicators.note: endlessly means the word for stylish loses its end letter

parts.note: chic means stylish

explanation.surface: A permanently fashionable person from Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' cuts the last C from CHIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: it is the 22nd letter of the Greek alphabet, written like an X.

clue.text: Single chap from east embracing old woman

indicators.note: the pieces embrace, hold inside, the letter for old
in an across clue, reading from the east means going right to left, so backwards

parts.note: a man is a chap
I, the Roman numeral one, means single

explanation.surface: An unmarried man from the Orient cuddling an elderly lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from east' reverses the chap, which then embraces O; the single letter goes on the end. 'old woman' looks like the definition but old supplies a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a woman's name, borne by the mother-in-law of Ruth in the Bible.

clue.text: Seedy soldiers kept in subject to argument

indicators.note: the soldiers are kept in, held inside, the word for arguable

parts.note: disputable means open to argument
RE, the Royal Engineers, are soldiers

explanation.surface: Shabby troops confined over a contested matter.
explanation.walkthrough: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: having a bad reputation, being shady or sleazy, is what seedy means here.
